brief: Weekly Morgan Stanley sales wrap covering a broad set of desk views. The September FOMC delivered a hawkish 25bp hike with no dissents; MS now forecasts two more 25bp hikes (December 2026, March 2027) to a 4.25-4.50% terminal range, a mentality shift toward a new hiking cycle that drove a bear-flattening sell-off in Financials even as bank NII/NIM guidance improved. Chief economist Gapen pivots his baseline to an oil risk premium, keeping core PCE inflation firmer (3.2% end-2026, 2.7% end-2027) and trimming 2027 GDP growth to 2.3%. Prime brokerage data shows funds net sold across regions this week, rotating from Momentum into Quality and from Semis/AI Tech into Hyperscalers/Cybersecurity, with US L/S leverage and gross exposure both up modestly. Europe's Eisenschmidt turns hawkish on the ECB (December hike call, deposit rate to 2.75%) while Japan's Yamaguchi brings forward the BoJ path to 1.50% by December. Separately, analysts argue AI capex is broadening beyond chips: Rachel Zhang frames it as a materials story (PCB/CCL demand multiples, tight glass fabric and copper foil supply), and Brian Nowak's Agentic Playbook names META, AAPL and AMZN as best-positioned horizontal platforms. The note also carries dozens of single-name rating and price-target changes across travel, autos, credit and tech.
